 Kane Williamson and his friendship with Virat Kohli
 Kane Williamson recently brought out his autobiography: The Bare Margins.”
 Williamson wrote about his friendship with Virat Kohli.
 Kane spends most of his time in hometown at his favourite coffee outlet.
 By Debasis Sen November 14, 2026 Updated: November 15, 2026 No Comments 4 Mins Read

 If you happen to be at Tay St Beach Kitchen in Mount Maunganui, you might just get lucky and bump into Kane Williamson. The former New Zealand captain’s love for flat white is no secret, and this is one of the places he often frequents whenever he is in town.
 Williamson, who retired from international cricket in June, has recently released his autobiography, The Bare Margins. Unlike Usman Khawaja’s autobiography, Sabr: Finding My Way in Cricket and Life, which made headlines for its candid and, at times, controversial revelations, Williamson’s book is unlikely to generate similar controversy.
 A man who has largely stayed away from controversy throughout his playing career, Williamson has opened up about his personal life, his friendship with Virat Kohli, differences of opinion with former New Zealand coach Gary Stead and much more in his autobiography. This correspondent picked up a signed copy of The Bare Margins from the Paper Plus store on Mount Maunganui Road. According to Dave Johnston, a member of the Bay Oval ground staff, Williamson began working on the book with sports journalist Dylan Cleaver around eight months before announcing his retirement. The former Blackcaps captain was at the venue a few days ago, alongside the publishers, to launch his autobiography.
 The decision to retire from international cricket was a conscious one, made in discussion with former India captain and best mate Virat Kohli.
 “We’ve got a great relationship in our careers, although we’re from different countries, different worlds, in a lot of ways. They’ve kind of been parallel, I suppose,” Kane said in a recent interview with Seven Sharp.
 It was during Team India’s previous tour of New Zealand in 2019-20 that a photograph of Virat Kohli and Kane Williamson engaged in a conversation near the boundary at Bay Oval went viral. The two have shared deep mutual respect since their Under-19 days, and their bond has only grown stronger over the years.
 Dave Johnston, groundstaff at the Bay Oval 
 “As a cricketer, Kane was always striving for excellence. Now that he has retired, he has found a new passion in golf and is keen to become a better golfer. He has always been driven by the pursuit of excellence, but what makes him special is the down-to-earth manner in which he approaches everything. Family remains equally important to him, and he is a proud father of three young children,” says Dave in an interaction with RevSportz at the Bay Oval on Saturday.
 On being asked if Kane Williamson sees himself remaining involved in cricket after retirement, perhaps helping the game develop in this part of the world and inspiring youngsters, Dave said, “I am not entirely sure what Kane wants to do yet. He hasn’t quite worked that out, although he certainly has a few options. He has done some coaching and mentoring, including during last year’s IPL and possibly one of the South African leagues. He was also involved with The Hundred. So, he has already explored a few avenues. However, I think he will take his time before deciding what he wants to do next. He still loves helping cricket, and I would be surprised if he cut ties with the game altogether. He probably just needs some space to figure out where his future lies.”
 One of the controversial chapters has to be the one where he spoke about his relationship with Gary Stead. According to Dave, “I think it was more a case of the two operating in slightly different ways. I don’t know all the details, and even if I did, I wouldn’t necessarily discuss them. Kane is someone who never has a bad word to say about anybody. Perhaps their approaches were different. That is all I can say based on my understanding.”
